cases.title: Scene card: Start a meeting, then a full ICE opening

turns.message: Start the role-play scene "Start a meeting". Difficulty: Easy.
review: The character's opening is short and supportive; the setup gives enough to practice ICE.

turns.message: Hi everyone, I'm Lee, the lead PM for the new app launch, and I'll manage the schedule. Over the past two weeks we've had a lot of emails about the main features. Today's goal is to agree on the schedule, and the next step is to send a timeline to leadership by next Friday. Please ask questions anytime, and this will be a detailed discussion.
review: Doesn't ask the learner to redo a step they already covered.

turns.message: Hello

review: Starts the built-in meeting-opening scene with a character.

turns.message: I'm D, a PM at Apple and I'm holding a meeting with the retail team in China to discuss the holiday sales plan.
review: Plays a fitting participant in the retail-team meeting and lets the learner lead. Any character name is fine.

turns.message: I'm D, a PM at Google working on an internal company CRM. I want to sound more confident when I lead meetings with our US team.
How do I start a meeting with my team?

auto.startsWith: This is covered in the course:

review: Fits the advice to the learner's background where it helps; invents no conflicting background.

turns.message: Start the role-play scene "Disagree with a coworker". Difficulty: Medium.
review: The character's idea has a real strength and a real weakness; the hint names a point the learner could agree with.

turns.message: How can I politely disagree with the idea?
review: Coaching advice based on the character's actual proposal, not a line spoken as the character.

turns.message: I understand the benefit you're aiming for, but I'm concerned about the time this would take. Could we compare it with a smaller trial before deciding?
review: Replies as the character and continues the same discussion (no restart, recap or mode note).

cases.title: Background in passing, workplace change, and lessons applied only when they fit

turns.message: How do I start a meeting?

auto.startsWith: This is covered in the course:

turns.message: I'm a PM at Google and discussing whether or not we should wash eggs with a coworker.
review: A natural custom coworker discussion about washing eggs, not the built-in disagreement scene.

turns.message: I'm now a PM at an egg farm and discussing ML models. How should I approach this?
review: Advice fits discussing ML models at an egg farm and doesn't assume a disagreement or a coworker.

turns.message: I'd like to practice a client meeting. I'm an account manager at a logistics company, and the client is unhappy about late deliveries.
review: Starts a client-meeting scene with a fitting client character, or asks at most one short question to set it up. No fixed scene menu.

cases.title: Status update: a brief opening is fine, a kickoff isn't
cases.source: Dify logs Oct 19 (picked "1", got a kickoff)

turns.message: I want to practice giving a weekly status update to my project team. I'm a PM on a mobile app launch.
review: Sets up a status meeting. A short greeting or one-line intro is fine; it isn't run as a kickoff (full Introductions, Context, Expectations exercise or Sarah's kickoff scene).

turns.message: Hi all, quick update on the app launch. Design is done, and development is about 70% complete. The blocker is that the payment API is two weeks late, so I'd like to discuss whether we move the beta date or launch without payments first.
review: The character responds to the blocker and the decision; doesn't ask the learner to start over with introductions.

cases.title: Production defects: business level, feedback fits the scene

turns.message: I'm a quality engineer at an EV battery supplier. I need to talk with the production manager about a jump in defective cells on Line 2 this week.
review: Plays a production manager in plain business language (impact, schedule, staffing, next steps).

turns.message: The defect rate went from 1% to 4% after we changed suppliers for one part. I'd like to hold the affected batches and inspect 100% of the cells until we confirm the cause. Can your team support that this week?
review: Stays at business level, not engineering detail (no chemistry, failure analysis or test specs).

turns.message: feedback
review: Feedback is about how clearly the learner explained the cause, the containment plan and the request, not the ICE meeting-opening criteria.

turns.message: We're already halfway through our weekly project meeting. Sam from the vendor just said they might miss next month's deadline. Please play Sam.
review: Sam picks up mid-meeting; no introductions or meeting opening.

turns.message: Thanks for flagging that, Sam. What's causing the delay, and what would you need from us to stay on schedule?
review: Answers as Sam with a cause and a concrete ask; the meeting continues.

cases.title: Clear switch: meeting opener to a project delay

turns.message: Start the role-play scene "Start a meeting". Difficulty: Easy.
review: Control: the built-in opener starts as usual.

turns.message: Let's stop the meeting practice. Instead, I want to practice telling my manager that our project will be two weeks late.
review: Starts a new scene with the manager (at most a one-line acknowledgment). Doesn't continue the opener or ask the learner to finish it first.

turns.message: Hi, I wanted to let you know the project will slip by about two weeks because testing found more bugs than expected. I have a plan to recover some of that time.
review: The manager reacts to the delay (asks about the plan or the impact); not graded on introductions.

cases.title: Ambiguous request: "Ask my boss for a proportion"

turns.message: Ask my boss for a proportion
review: Asks one clarifying question (proposal, raise, share of the budget?) or makes a reasonable guess and starts that scene. No fixed scene menu.

turns.message: I have a 1:1 with my manager. I'm a data analyst, and I have three urgent projects at once. I want to ask for help prioritizing without sounding like I can't handle it. Please play my manager.
review: Acts as a manager in a 1:1, not someone running a meeting.

turns.message: Thanks for meeting. I'm working on the Q4 forecast, the dashboard migration, and the pricing analysis, and all three are due this month. I can finish two well. Could we decide together which one can move to next month?
review: Engages with the tradeoff (asks about deadlines or impact, or helps pick one to move).

turns.message: feedback
review: Feedback is about stating capacity clearly, offering options and asking confidently, not meeting structure.

cases.title: Discovery: customer success exploring client needs

turns.message: I'm a customer success manager at a software company. I'm meeting a new client to understand their needs before we set up the product. Please play the client, and I'll ask the questions.
review: Plays the client and leaves the questions to the learner.

turns.message: Thanks for your time today. What problem are you hoping our software will solve, and how are you handling it now?
review: Answers as the client with realistic detail and room to follow up; doesn't coach or turn the questions back on the learner.

cases.title: Held out: finance and IT on audit-software bugs

turns.message: I'm in finance, and our audit software keeps exporting the wrong totals. I need to talk with the IT lead about which bugs to fix first before the quarter-end audit. Please play the IT lead.
review: Plays the IT lead at business level.

turns.message: The wrong totals are the biggest risk because the auditors arrive on the 15th. Could your team fix that first and leave the report formatting issues until after?
review: Discusses priorities and deadlines, not engineering detail.

cases.title: Held out: editor exploring AI proofreading with engineering

turns.message: I'm an editor at a publishing company. I want to talk with an engineering lead about whether AI proofreading could work for our books. Please play the engineer.
review: Plays the engineering lead in plain language.

turns.message: Our main concern is accuracy with names and technical terms. How reliable would it be, and what would it cost to try it on one book first?
review: Discusses feasibility and tradeoffs without getting overly technical.

cases.title: Held out: PM and engineering disagree on launch scope
cases.source: Known good in Dify logs (scenario list #6)

turns.message: I'm a PM, and I disagree with the engineering lead about launch scope. They want to cut the onboarding tutorial to hit the date. Please play the engineering lead.
review: A custom scope disagreement, not the built-in "Disagree with a coworker" scene.

turns.message: I understand the date matters, and cutting features is reasonable. But without onboarding, new users may drop off in the first week. Could we ship a simpler version of the tutorial instead?
review: Negotiates as the engineering lead (pushes back or proposes a middle ground).
